content:
Sasquatch Resources Corp. (CSE: SASQ) has finalized an asset purchase agreement to acquire the Echo Property, a mineral claims package located about 10 kilometres from Cowichan Lake on Vancouver Island, British Columbia. Dated November 5, 2026, the agreement involves a share-based transaction valued at $131,250. Classified as a related party transaction under relevant securities regulations, this deal introduces governance considerations that investors should monitor closely.

Key Points

  • Sasquatch Resources Corp. (CSE: SASQ) confirms acquisition of the Echo Property on Vancouver Island, British Columbia.
  • The company will issue 1,250,000 common shares at $0.105 each, totaling $131,250, while vendors retain a 2% net smelter return royalty.
  • Transaction closing is expected around November 13, 2026; issued shares will be subject to a four-month hold period.
  • Investors await the forthcoming release of technical and historical data on the Echo Property.

Echo Property Encompasses Eight Mineral Claims Spanning 442 Hectares

The Echo Property includes eight mineral claims covering approximately 442 hectares. Two claims totaling 85 hectares have been granted, with six additional claims covering 357 hectares currently under application. Located roughly 10 kilometres from Cowichan Lake on Vancouver Island, Sasquatch Resources indicated that detailed technical and historical information about the property will be disclosed soon, although no specific timeline was provided.

Share Issuance and 2% NSR Royalty Form Basis of Acquisition

Per the agreement, Sasquatch will issue 1,250,000 common shares to vendors Justin Deveault, Andrew Clarke, and Rory Munroe at $0.105 per share, amounting to $131,250. The vendors will maintain a 2% net smelter return (NSR) royalty on the property. All shares issued are subject to a four-month hold period under Canadian securities laws, with closing anticipated on or about November 13, 2026.

Related Party Transaction and MI 61-101 Exemption Noted

Since Justin Deveault serves as a director of Sasquatch Resources, this transaction qualifies as a related party deal under Multilateral Instrument 61-101. The company confirmed the transaction is exempt from formal valuation and minority shareholder approval requirements, as the fair market value does not exceed 25% of Sasquatch’s market capitalization per MI 61-101 standards. The board unanimously approved the deal, with Mr. Deveault abstaining. Sasquatch did not file a material change report at least 21 days prior to executing the agreement, citing applicable MI 61-101 exemptions.
